title: Shattrath City
body: Shattrath, whose name means dwelling of light, was once the capital of the draenei on this world. When the Burning Legion turned the orcs against them, the fiercest battle of that war was fought here, and the city fell. For years it lay in ruin and darkness, until the naaru called the Sha'tar came to Outland to fight the demons and were drawn to these ruins, where a small remnant of the draenei priesthood still held its rites. Those priests, the Aldor, regained their strength, and rebuilding began. Later a host of blood elves sent by Kael'thas marched on the city and instead knelt before the naaru A'dal, becoming the Scryers. Today it rises in northwestern Terokkar Forest, perhaps the one place in Outland with any semblance of safety. A'dal holds the Terrace of Light at its heart, the two rival orders keep their own heights above it, and refugees of every race crowd the Lower City. Portals link it to the capitals of Azeroth, and from here the Sha'tar make war on the Legion and its allies.

title: Terrace of Light
body: The Terrace of Light is the heart of Shattrath and the seat of the Sha'tar. In the chamber at its center floats A'dal, leader of the naaru, with Khadgar close at hand, and around the hall stand portals to the capitals of the Alliance and the Horde. Grand Anchorite Almonen preaches here that the Light dwells within each of us as a gift, given freely to all, and that those who heed it grow in its power. Spymistress Mehlisah Highcrown speaks for the Lower City, urging that Auchindoun be cleared of the Shadow Council before a worse disaster than the Bone Wastes befalls them. The Aldor and the Scryers each keep a bank on the terrace's rim.

parts.body: In these days the terrace also serves the Shattered Sun Offensive. Beneath A'dal stands an image of the Sunwell's defenses, and General Tiras'alan of the Offensive studies it closely, sending those willing to fight on to the Isle of Quel'Danas, north of Quel'Thalas.

title: Lower City
body: The Lower City is the lowest ring of Shattrath and the home of its refugees. As one of the only safe havens in Outland, the city draws them from every war, past and present: Broken and Lost Ones, sporelings and Mag'har, high elves, dwarves, orcs and human peasants, and arakkoa outcasts who turned from Skettis. Every spare building now houses them; the rogue Lonika Stillblade has even closed her academy. Khadgar warns newcomers to watch for pickpockets. It is a busy market too: Griftah swears by his miraculous amulets, and the arakkoa alchemist Lorokeem keeps his strange equipment in the northwest.

parts.body: Since the war against the Lich King began, the Lower City has sent soldiers to Northrend as well. Two battle-mages keep their posts here, Arcanist Iramhir of the Silver Covenant for the Alliance and Magistrix Aldessia of the Sunreavers for the Horde, and each sends fighters north to the war for Wintergrasp.

title: World's End Tavern
body: At the eastern edge of the Lower City stands the World's End Tavern, where Shaarubo tends the bar and the barmaid Kylene cooks enough to fill the ogre Grok. Its regulars are a strange lot. The mo'arg Sal'salabim drinks away his sorrows, Raliq the Drunk bellows at all comers, and the socialite Haris Pilton holds court with her pet while an ex-socialite lingers close by. Lonika Stillblade waits here for a new home for her rogue academy. Just outside, Wind Trader Lathrai admits the tavern offers nothing to his kind, though its patrons buy his wares.

parts.body: Of late a stranger named Zephyr has joined the regulars, a representative of the Keepers of Time who will carry those his order trusts to the Caverns of Time. This world, he muses, has been damaged in ways beyond what eyes can see, and even the passage of time feels different here.

title: Aldor Rise
body: Aldor Rise is the highest tier of Shattrath and the home of the Aldor, the draenei priesthood that kept its rites among the ruins until the naaru came. On its western side stands the Shrine of Unending Light, their most holy temple, where the Light is said to burn strongly enough to cleanse even the foulest fel taint, and where High Priestess Ishanah receives those who join the order. Adyen the Lightwarden keeps watch over the priesthood, vindicators guard the paths, and anchorites and neophytes train among the dwellings. An inn on the southern side offers rest. As a holy site the rise welcomes only the initiated, and those who side with the Scryers find no friends here.

title: Scryer's Tier
body: Scryer's Tier is the raised platform where the Scryers make their home, the blood elves who abandoned Kael'thas for the naaru. Arcane guardians and arcanists watch over its walks, and only those initiated with the Scryers are welcome. In the Seer's Library on its southwestern side sits their leader, Voren'thal the Seer, who means the library to make a seer out of everyone. An inn on the eastern side, enchanters, merchants and a fence serve the order's members. The Aldor take little joy in sharing the city with them, for many priests died at the hands of these very magisters.

parts.body: In these days the Seer's Library has a keeper of its own. Beside Voren'thal, Loremaster Skosiris tends what he calls perhaps the greatest depository of lore in all of Outland, and he claims that even the grand libraries of Silvermoon City pale beside it.

title: A'dal
body: A'dal is the leader of the Sha'tar, the naaru who reclaimed Shattrath, and he rules the city from the Terrace of Light. He speaks without words: those who approach feel a soothing light and hear slow chimes in their minds, and with them comes the assurance that they are safe. Khadgar warns visitors not to trouble him with petty questions, for his will alone keeps the city's enemies from crushing it. Each day he chooses which rival order joins Xi'ri in Shadowmoon Valley, and the armies take his blessing before they march.

parts.body: When a champion survived the battle at Crimson Watch and brought A'dal word of the Crimson Sigil, Illidan's elite, the naaru promised that the Sigil would be investigated, for it threatens all life on Draenor. He foresaw a day when its dark master would have to answer for his crimes, and wondered whether the one before him would be the one to bring him to justice.

title: Khadgar
body: Khadgar was apprentice to Medivh, the Last Guardian, and it was he who learned that his master had been possessed by Sargeras and had opened the Dark Portal; though he honored Medivh, he slew him. After fighting beside Anduin Lothar, he went into Draenor with Turalyon, Alleria, Danath and Kurdran as the Sons of Lothar, and as that world tore apart they shattered the portal behind them. Trapped in Outland, he sensed the Burning Legion closing in, reached into the Great Dark Beyond, and found A'dal and his naaru. He says he convinced them to come. Now he stands by A'dal, swearing he has learned more from A'dal in five months than in all his years among Dalaran's libraries.

title: High Priestess Ishanah
body: Ishanah is the High Priestess of the Aldor, the draenei priests who serve the Sha'tar, and she receives new allies in the Shrine of Unending Light. It was the Aldor who named the naaru Sha'tar, born from light. Her people were charged with guarding the holy sites of this land, and she grieves that so many altars now lie ruined or defiled. Turning refugees away, she says, would be hypocrisy. Of the Scryers she is blunter: she does not like them or their leader's wild claims of visions of redemption, but it is not for her to question the wisdom of the naaru, and in such times allies must be taken where they are found.

title: Voren'thal the Seer
body: Voren'thal the Seer was once a close advisor to Prince Kael'thas, until visions warned him that the prince's path would lead the blood elves to ruin. When Kael sent a regiment to lay waste to Shattrath, Voren'thal was its leader. On the bridge before the Terrace of Light his soldiers laid down their arms, and he strode in to kneel before A'dal, declaring that he had seen the naaru in a vision and that his race's only hope lay with him. Many of Kael's finest scholars and magisters followed him. Now he keeps the Seer's Library on Scryer's Tier, where truth is brought to light, while his alchemists brew elixirs to sharpen his often clouded visions.

title: Adyen the Lightwarden
body: Adyen the Lightwarden is the sword of the Aldor. He describes his duty plainly: first to protect the priesthood at all costs, and second to destroy the enemies of the Light wherever they hide. From Aldor Rise he asks those who would prove themselves to bring him the insignias of the Burning Legion and the Shadow Council, from the lesser marks of Kil'jaeden carried in the Bone Wastes, Nagrand and Blade's Edge to the marks of Sargeras worn by the Legion's officers in Netherstorm and Shadowmoon Valley. He reminds them what the Aldor are, keepers of the Light and servants of the naaru, and what stands against them.

parts.body: In time a new summons reached the Aldor Rise: a crisis at the Sunwell Plateau, on the Isle of Quel'Danas in Azeroth. His forces were already spread thin, but the Lightwarden sent every soldier he could spare to answer it, and wished he could send more.

title: Magistrix Fyalenn
body: Magistrix Fyalenn of the Scryers has no regrets: leaving Kael'thas, she says, was the best thing any of them ever did, for his followers are too blind or too frightened to see where he is leading them. The prince sees the Scryers as a threat to his hold over other blood elves and has tried to crush them time and again, and few sin'dorei fresh from Silvermoon are willing to keep the company Kael now keeps. Scryers and Kael's armies attack each other on sight. To Fyalenn the only proof of loyalty is fighting, and she asks for the signets of the Firewing and the higher-ranking Sunfury taken from Kael's soldiers across Outland.

title: Sha'nir
body: Sha'nir is an Aldor healer who tends the injured refugees laid out in the city's infirmary. More arrive every day, some so badly hurt it is a wonder they made it. She cares nothing for the politics of the city and takes help from Aldor or Scryer alike; she is so short of hands, she says, that she would not turn away an ogre who knew how to apply a tourniquet. Poison wounds trouble her most, for her antivenom runs low. Beside her rests Zahlia, blinded by a blow to the head, whom Sha'nir hopes to cure with the blood of an ancient basilisk she has known of since she was a youngling.

title: Rilak the Redeemed
body: Rilak the Redeemed leads the arakkoa who have made a home in the northern Lower City. He speaks of his race without pride: too often, he admits, the arakkoa have turned dark magic to wicked ends, and it was through A'dal that he learned of the Light and of redemption. Skettis marks outcasts such as his for death, so Rilak watches Terokk's city closely and shares what he knows with those who would strike at it, and frontier garrisons plagued by arakkoa raids send envoys to him.

title: Yuula
body: Yuula is the recruitment officer of the Sha'tari Skyguard, and she does her recruiting in Shattrath itself. The Skyguard is sworn to protect the city from the dangers that loom above it, near and far. Her first concern is close to home: the Gordunni ogres of the Barrier Hills to the north, a threat that Shattrath's soldiers on the ground have struggled to reach, and the riders of the Skyguard are the ones who can. Those who help contain them earn a hearty welcome as an ace and hear of the Skyguard's greater war beyond the Skethyl Mountains.

title: Barthamus
body: Barthamus is a nether drake of the Netherwing who waits in the Lower City with six of his kin, Jorus, Malfas, Onyxien, Suraku, Voranaku and Zoya. Far from Shadowmoon Valley, where the Dragonmaw clan holds his flight's old sanctuary and rides its captured young, the seven keep to a quiet corner among the refugees. They have little to say to passing strangers. They seem to be waiting for someone in particular, though they do not say who.

parts.body: Barthamus calls himself the first of his flight, the abandoned child of a monster. To the highlord who survived meeting Illidan and came back to him, he owes everything: that one hero shattered the Dragonmaw's hold and brought back secrets enough to occupy his brethren for ten lifetimes. In thanks each of his kin offers to bond with the hero and fly them across Outland, though only one may be chosen, and that choice cannot be undone.

title: City of Light
body: Newcomers to Shattrath soon hear its story. A haggard war veteran calls the city perhaps the one place in Outland with any semblance of safety, since the naaru called the Sha'tar drove the demons away, and he sends strangers to see A'dal on the Terrace of Light. Khadgar, beside the naaru, warns them not to burden A'dal with petty questions and, too busy discussing strategy to guide them himself, summons a servant to lead the way. Shattrath, the servant explains, was the capital of the draenei and fell in the fiercest battle of the orcs' war against them. It lay dark until the Sha'tar came and found a remnant of the priesthood, the Aldor, keeping their rites in a ruined temple, which now serves as an infirmary.

parts.body: The Aldor grew strong and rebuilding began. Then Kael'thas sent a regiment of blood elves to destroy the city. On the bridge they laid down their arms, and their leader Voren'thal knelt before A'dal. The defectors became the Scryers, though the Aldor, whose priests those same magisters had slain, have never warmed to them. Xi'ri has since carried the war to Illidan's doorstep, and the orders vie to join him. To serve the Sha'tar, the servant warns, a newcomer must choose between them.
sources: creature_text 19685 groups 7 to 20 (the second half of the tour)

title: The Aldor's Charge
body: Those who would stand with the Aldor find the priesthood's work everywhere. In the city, the healer Sha'nir needs venom sacs from the dreadfang spiders of the southeast to make antidotes for refugees who survived the road only to die of their wounds. Outside the walls, High Priestess Ishanah sends her allies east to an arakkoa outpost deliberately built atop three of the Aldor's sacred altars, carrying a blessed vial to cleanse each one, for the Aldor are keepers of the Light. She asks too for fel armaments taken from demons, to show the power of her temple. From Adyen the Lightwarden comes the war itself: the insignias of Kil'jaeden and of Sargeras, stripped from the Legion and the Shadow Council across Outland. The Aldor's reach goes further still, to the anchorites under Exarch Orelis watching Kael'thas in Netherstorm.

parts.body: Brought into the Shrine of Unending Light, one of the holiest places in all of Outland, a fel armament does not last long. Ishanah bids its bearer watch as the foul materials disintegrate and the metal turns to dust, until the fel is gone from this world and only the pure residue of the Light remains.

notes: Converted: the story was over the 140-word opening limit, so the cleansing of the fel armaments moved to part 1 (DONE 10420, needs Aldor Neutral or better); the opening keeps Ishanah's request. 'Each mark a measure of the order's trust' and 'cannot forsake their charge even now' trimmed for length. requiredState 8. Together every character can begin the story at some point. The Scryer counterpart is 370318. Netherstorm's Orelis chain is only mentioned.

title: The Seer's Visions
body: The Scryers serve the naaru by seeing what others cannot. Voren'thal's visions are vague and unfocused, so his alchemists brew an elixir to sharpen them, and Arcanist Adyria, whose ethereal supplier has failed her, sends any willing helper after the eyes of dampscale basilisks in the rocky lands of Terokkar; those visions, she says, may one day decide the fate of their race. The order's war is fought in the open as well. Magistrix Fyalenn demands the signets of Kael's Firewing soldiers and of his higher-ranking Sunfury as proof of loyalty, since the prince's armies and the Scryers strike at each other on sight. Voren'thal himself seeks arcane tomes, most often carried by Kael's blood elves, for the power within them. His spies reach far, too: Spymaster Thalodien's team in Netherstorm has found something of great importance.

parts.body: An arcane tome is no ordinary book on arcane matters: there is power in it. Brought to the Seer's Library, a tome is condensed by Voren'thal, the whole of its raw power drawn into a single arcane rune. The power is tremendous, he says, yet one with a clear mind condenses it easily.

notes: Converted: the story was over the 140-word opening limit, so what Voren'thal does with the tomes moved to part 1 (DONE 10416, needs Scryers Neutral or better); the opening keeps his request. Thalodien's call for reinforcements shortened. requiredState 8. Before: Fact-check: 10024 needs Scryers below Neutral (draenei before choosing and Aldor-aligned characters), 10412 needs Scryers Neutral to Honored, 10416 needs Scryers Neutral or better; together every character can begin it. 'Kael's own magisters' changed to Kael's blood elves (10416). Aldor counterpart 370317. Thalodien's chain belongs to netherstorm.json and is only mentioned.

title: Lives in the Lower City
body: Not every tale in Shattrath is one of war. In the Lower City, a boy named Seth, far from his home in Lakeshire, watches the Aldor rebuild the walls and decides they work far faster than old Foreman Oslow ever did; he misses fishing for eels at a lake to the northeast, but his mother says it is too dangerous now. Nearby the arakkoa outcast Vekax cannot set foot outside the walls, for Skettis has marked him for death, so he pays in treasure for the feathers of its servants as proof that the outcasts will not take their punishment lying down. And the fishmonger Oloraak frets over his friend Isfar, who escaped the Sethekk Halls once and has gone back alone to free his sister, ignoring every plea to stay safe in the city.

title: The Trials of the Naaru
body: Tempest Keep, the fortress where Prince Kael'thas holds court in Netherstorm, has drawn the eye of A'dal. Its satellites, the Mechanar, the Botanica, the Arcatraz and the Eye, ring the prince's seat, and from the Terrace of Light the naaru means in time to send champions against them and to bring the prince to account. Those who serve the Sha'tar find their way into his plans by more than one road. Khadgar, for one, sends those who have proven capable of great feats before the naaru, for A'dal seeks adventurers willing to undergo trials, and those who prove their strength will be granted his favor.

parts.body: One road began at the Stormspire. Nexus-Prince Haramad, an ethereal of his word, gave the ata'mal crystal to the one whose heroics had recovered it, to be handed to the naaru, and lent his own teleporter so that it could be carried straight to A'dal on the Terrace of Light.

A'dal knew the crystal at once: Spirit's Song, the ata'mal crystal Prophet Velen left with his people for safekeeping before his ill-fated mission to the Exodar. Odd, the naaru mused, that Velen had not foreseen it falling to the Legion, even for a short time. Or perhaps he had, and left it there so that it would be recovered and brought here.

Haramad had hidden a message inside the crystal, vital to the campaign against Tempest Keep. The key to its Arcatraz satellite lies in two shards, one held by the ancient Warp Splinter in the Botanica, the other by Pathaleon the Calculator in the Mechanar, and A'dal would join them into one.
sources: quest 10704 description (offered at once after 10280: RewardNextQuest)

parts.body: A'dal forged the key, and soon there was need of it. A discordant note crept into the naaru's voice: Kael'thas had chosen his warden poorly, and the beings the naaru once locked away in the Arcatraz were breaking free. One of them, Harbinger Skyriss, a servant of the Old Gods, sought to bring about his masters' conquest of every world.

Khadgar's news concerned the prince himself. The discovery of the Cipher of Damnation had shown that Kael'thas was involved, and should Kael use the cipher, Khadgar warned, what little is left of this world might collapse. A'dal is convinced that the prince must be stopped.

Tempest Keep is a naaru creation, A'dal answered, and the way into it has always been theirs to grant. They go now because they must, for Kael'thas cannot be allowed to utter the words of damnation, but only a fool would enter unproven. Four trials he set, and three came first: mercy, saving three prisoners from execution at the hands of Kargath Bladefist in the Shattered Halls; strength, against Warlord Kalithresh and Murmur; and tenacity, rescuing the hapless gnome Millhouse Manastorm from the Arcatraz.
sources: quests 10884, 10885, 10886 descriptions (offered by A'dal once 10883 is done; each begins 'Four trials you must pass')

parts.body: Those who passed the first three trials learned the last. Only one obstacle remained: an army had to be gathered and led deep inside Hellfire Citadel, to fight its way to the heart of Magtheridon's lair and destroy the foul corrupter.

title: Akama's Promise
body: With the Medallion of Karabor whole at last, Akama will not keep it. Years spent so close to evil itself, he fears, have weakened him, and he no longer trusts himself with an artifact of such power. He sets the ata'mal crystal into the medallion and hands it to the one who recovered it, to carry to the one being he knows can be trusted with it, A'dal in Shattrath City. The gift is also his promise: when the time comes to face Illidan, Akama will stand on its bearer's side. Until then he and his Deathsworn keep up the mask they show the Betrayer, with Maiev Shadowsong hidden among them in the Warden's Cage.

parts.body: Given to A'dal, the medallion vanished into the naaru's being in a flash of light, and its bearer was shown a glimpse of a moment, perhaps one yet to come: Akama and Maiev coming out of the Warden's Cage and fighting their way toward the temple, aided by a third figure shrouded in shadow. Looking closer, the bearer saw that the figure was themselves.

The plan was nearly undone. Seer Olum, freed from naga who had learned he worked against Illidan, had told his torturers nothing, for Akama himself taught him to master pain. But Illidan had asked for Olum to be brought before him, and the Betrayer would have seen into his soul's deepest secrets. Akama had to be warned.

Olum gave his life to keep the secret, a sacrifice Akama says he would never have asked of him. To lull Illidan back into a false sense of security, Akama would do the Betrayer's bidding for now: wearing a magical cowl that made them seem one of his Ashtongue, his ally was to slay Kael's phoenix, Al'ar, in Tempest Keep.

With Al'ar slain, Illidan's attention turned to Kael'thas, and Akama made his move. A vision had shown him the phylactery of the lich Rage Winterchill, whose power was lost when the lich fell in the Battle of Mount Hyjal. Legend spoke of a place guarded by bronze dragons, where past and present meet: in the Caverns of Time the phylactery could still be won.
sources: quest 10947 description (offered at once after 10946: RewardNextQuest)

parts.body: With the phylactery in hand, Akama told why he had hidden his intentions so long instead of siding openly with the naaru. His very soul is held prisoner inside the Black Temple, and Illidan could destroy him at any moment. The phylactery's power over souls will let him reclaim it, and now he will lead Maiev and his Deathsworn to Illidan's doorstep, if A'dal will strike with them.

A'dal answered with an image: a naaru outside the Black Temple, fighting beside draenei vindicators and blood elf magisters. Xi'ri's army of Aldor and Scryers pushed Illidan's forces back to cover Akama and Maiev as they entered the temple, and the medallion returned to its bearer, its power augmented by the naaru's magic, as the key to the Black Temple.
sources: quest 10985 description, objectives and reward text

title: The Offensive in Outland
body: While the Shattered Sun Offensive fights on Quel'Danas, its officers in Shattrath keep the war fed from Outland. Emissary Mordin collects nether residue, found by herbalists, miners and skinners across Outland, for oils that colleagues in Stormwind make to harden the troops' blades and armor; no contribution, he says, is too small. Lord Torvos learned that Kael'thas had ordered the Sunfury of Netherstorm to strike the Offensive's Outland operations, to draw its strength away from the Sunwell, and he wants their attack plans seized. Harbinger Haronem, under orders to investigate anything that might help, grudgingly sends volunteers to the Spirit Fields of Nagrand with goggles to take readings of strange distortions, all at the insistence of the gnome Whirligig Wafflefry, who is busy hawking gadgets derived from the Offensive's military inventions.
